title: arXiv physics daily — 2026-11-26 announcement batch: 8 notable papers
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. The supplied signal file has no candidate-level records or paper-specific attention values, so this is a notable-paper ordering from the latest available 2026-11-26 batch, not a measured popularity ranking; citation evidence for these recent preprints is limited.

sections.title: Experimental Quantum Hardware Benchmarks of Flat Non-Clifford Hypergraph States, Antipodal Obstructions, and Nonlocal Games on IBM Heron r2
sections.abstract: The authors test non-Clifford hypergraph-state structure and contextuality-style games on two IBM Heron r2 processors, reporting hardware benchmarks across 3–50 qubits.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report non-Clifford coherence and multiple game/witness violations on IBM Heron r2, including a 96.85% raw Mermin–Peres win rate on one backend and parity-game violations up to 30 qubits.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; 11 IBM Heron r2 jobs on ibm_fez and ibm_kingston, using 4,096 shots per circuit
sections.unique_caveat: The authors say the single-chip runs do not close the relativistic locality loophole; finite shots and routing/depth limitations constrain some higher-qubit tests.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: No per-paper attention values were present in the supplied signal file, which had no candidate records. Included for direct hardware evidence across two processors, auditable jobs, and a connection between non-Clifford witnesses and quantum nonlocality tests.

sections.title: Unfreezing topology using out-of-equilibrium replica exchanges
sections.abstract: The authors introduce a gradual, out-of-equilibrium replica-exchange method for mitigating topological freezing and test it in a two-dimensional CP^{N−1} lattice model.
sections.claimed_result: For the tested N=21 model, authors report at least about 40% lower computational cost at fixed statistical precision than standard parallel tempering on boundary conditions, across five lattice spacings.
sections.evidence_type: computational; simulations of the two-dimensional CP^{N−1} model with N=21, compared with standard replica exchange
sections.unique_caveat: The quantitative demonstration is restricted to this model and setup; the paper frames extension to four-dimensional gauge theories as future work.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: No per-paper attention values were available in the supplied signal file. Cross-listed between lattice field theory and statistical mechanics, the work derives an acceptance/cost model and checks it against simulations rather than presenting only a proposed algorithm.

sections.title: Bound Entanglement with Negative Partial Transpose Exists
sections.abstract: The author gives an explicit Werner state on C^8 ⊗ C^8 that is negative under partial transpose yet nondistillable by LOCC, with a further fidelity bound under separable operations.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves that the specified state is NPT and bound entangled, and that separable operations cannot produce a two-qubit Bell-state fidelity above (1+√2)/4 ≈ 0.604.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; exact analysis of a specified 8×8 Werner state, with a computer-assisted search used to find a proof certificate that the paper then checks exactly
sections.unique_caveat: This is a mathematical existence result for a particular state, not an experimental preparation or a general classification of NPT states.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: No per-paper attention values were emitted for this item. Its four-way cross-list and explicit finite-dimensional theorem make it a concrete connection across quantum information, condensed matter, complexity, and information theory.

sections.title: Probing Dynamical Dark Energy with Hyper Suprime-Cam Year 3 Cosmic Shear
sections.abstract: The authors combine HSC Year 3 cosmic shear with distance probes to test constant and time-varying dark-energy models, finding a 2.4σ preference for evolution in the latter parameterization.
sections.claimed_result: In the authors' joint w0waCDM analysis, w0=−0.832^{+0.071}_{−0.059} and wa=−1.23^{+0.66}_{−0.44}, a 2.4σ preference for dynamical dark energy; the reported S8 constraint remains consistent with their baseline HSC ΛCDM result.
sections.evidence_type: observational; HSC-Y3 real-space cosmic-shear correlations with DESI DR2 BAO, DES five-year supernova data, and BBN priors
sections.unique_caveat: The authors say the dynamical-dark-energy preference is driven primarily by the geometric distance probes, not by the lensing amplitude alone; it is not a discovery-level result.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: No per-paper attention record was available. Included for a reported measurement using over 25 million galaxies across 416 deg² and an explicit comparison of weak-lensing constraints with external distance data.

sections.title: State of the UNIONS: Four Milky Way companions discovered in a systematic search for northern Local Group satellites
sections.abstract: A systematic search of UNIONS g,r,i imaging identifies four faint Milky Way satellite systems, two of which are candidate ultra-faint dwarf galaxies.
sections.claimed_result: The authors identify Boötes VI and Draco III as likely ultra-faint dwarf galaxies and report two still fainter, compact systems named UNIONS 2 and UNIONS 3.
sections.evidence_type: observational; systematic search of Ultraviolet Near-Infrared Optical Northern Survey imaging
sections.unique_caveat: Boötes VI and Draco III still need chemodynamical confirmation; morphology alone cannot determine whether UNIONS 2 and 3 are dark-matter-dominated galaxies.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: No candidate-level attention values were available. Included for four survey discoveries with measured luminosity/size estimates and a clear distinction between candidate galaxies and unclassified faint systems.

sections.title: Measuring the flavor composition of high-energy neutrinos from the Milky Way
sections.abstract: The author forecasts that IceCube and KM3NeT may resolve the flavor composition of Galactic high-energy neutrinos in roughly a decade, potentially distinguishing source and propagation scenarios.
sections.claimed_result: The author estimates future telescopes could infer the source νe fraction to within 27%; a comparison of Galactic and extragalactic flavor compositions could test strong source magnetic fields or neutrino decay.
sections.evidence_type: forecast/proposal; projected sensitivity for IceCube and KM3NeT, which view the inner Galaxy from complementary hemispheres
sections.unique_caveat: This is a forecast, not a flavor measurement; the timeline and precision depend on future exposure and source/propagation assumptions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: No per-paper attention record was emitted. The four-archive cross-list and a quantitative forecast connect Galactic astrophysics with neutrino detection and particle phenomenology.

sections.title: Signals from the early Universe: primordial features from the full-shape analysis of BOSS galaxies and eBOSS quasars in combination with Planck
sections.abstract: The authors search for oscillatory primordial features in Planck CMB and BOSS/eBOSS large-scale-structure data using multiple templates and find no statistically significant evidence.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report no significant detection: the best LSS fits improve χ² by about 6–10 but reach at most 1.6σ global significance after the look-elsewhere correction; the strongest CMB-only feature is about 2.6σ.
sections.evidence_type: observational; Planck PR4, BOSS galaxy clustering, and eBOSS quasar clustering analyzed with one-loop effective field theory of large-scale structure
sections.unique_caveat: The LSS amplitude bounds are 1.4–3 times weaker than Planck's over the tested frequencies, and the combined constraints do not strengthen the CMB result because the preferred frequencies do not align.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: No per-paper attention values were available. Included for a joint CMB/galaxy/quasar analysis using full-shape power-spectrum multipoles and an explicit look-elsewhere-adjusted assessment of candidate features.

sections.title: Nuclear Modification of π⁰ Production in pO and OO Collisions with ALICE
sections.abstract: The contribution reports neutral-pion nuclear-modification measurements in proton–oxygen and oxygen–oxygen collisions, intended to separate cold- and hot-nuclear-matter effects.
sections.claimed_result: The author reports presenting R_pO and R_OO measurements at √sNN=9.62 TeV and 5.36 TeV respectively, using ALICE π⁰ transverse-momentum spectra.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; ALICE electromagnetic-calorimeter π⁰ spectra in pO, OO, and pp collisions
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract does not provide numerical modification-factor values or uncertainties, so the magnitude of the reported effects cannot be assessed from the abstract alone.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: No per-paper attention values were available. Included as an experimental measurement in pO/OO systems, comparing their spectra with pp data and with models containing cold and hot matter effects.
